title.en: Volume 214 Biographies 102: Yang Bo, Ma Sen, Liu Tigan, Wang Ting, Ge Shouli, Jin Xueyan
title.raw: 卷二百十四 列傳第一百〇二 楊博 馬森 劉體乾 王廷 葛守禮 靳學顏 Volume 214 Biographies 102: Yang Bo, Ma Sen, Liu Tigan, Wang Ting, Ge Shouli, Jin Xueyan

sentences.zh: 楊博

translations.literal: Yang Bo
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo

sentences.zh: 〈（子俊民）〉

translations.literal: (son Junmin)〉
translations.idiomatic: (son Junmin)〉

sentences.zh: 馬森劉體乾王廷

translations.literal: Ma Sen, Liu Tigan, Wang Ting
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sen, Liu Tigan, and Wang Ting

translations.literal: (Mao Kai)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Mao Kai)〉

sentences.zh: 葛守禮靳學顏

translations.literal: Ge Shouli, Jin Xueyan
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shouli and Jin Xueyan

sentences.zh: 〈（弟學曾）〉

translations.literal: (younger brother Xuezeng)〉
translations.idiomatic: (younger brother Xuezeng)〉

sentences.zh: 楊博，字惟約，蒲州人。

translations.literal: Yang Bo, styled Weiyue, was a man of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo, styled Weiyue, was a native of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父瞻，御史，終四川僉事。

translations.literal: His father Zhan was a censor and ended as Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Zhan served as a censor and ended his career as Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 博登嘉靖八年進士，除盩啡知縣，調長安。

translations.literal: Bo passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Jiajing, was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi, and was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bo passed the jinshi examinations in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign (1529), was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi, and was then transferred to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 征為兵部武庫主事，歷職方郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be a secretary in the Armory Bureau of the Ministry of War and rose to director in the Operations Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a secretary in the Armory Bureau of the Ministry of War and rose through the ranks to become a director in the Operations Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大學士翟鑾巡九邊，以博自隨。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan inspected the Nine Frontier Circuits and took Bo with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Zhai Luan inspected the Nine Frontier Circuits, he took Bo along with him.

sentences.zh: 所過山川形勢，土俗好惡，士卒多寡強弱，皆疏記之。

translations.literal: Wherever they passed, the terrain, local customs, and the numbers and strength of the troops were all recorded in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere they went, he recorded in memorials the lay of the land, local customs, and how many troops there were and how strong they were.

sentences.zh: 至肅州，屬番數百遮道邀賞。

translations.literal: At Suzhou, several hundred dependent tribesmen blocked the road seeking rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Suzhou, several hundred dependent tribesmen blocked the road demanding gifts.

sentences.zh: 鑾慮來者益眾，不能給。

translations.literal: Zhai feared that more would come and that they could not be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai worried that still more would arrive and that they could not afford to reward them all.

sentences.zh: 博請鑾盛儀衛，集諸番轅門外，數以天子宰相至，不悉眾遠迎，將縛以屬吏。

translations.literal: Bo asked Zhai to display full ceremonial guard, assemble the tribesmen outside the camp gate, and rebuke them that the Son of Heaven's chief minister had come yet they had not all come far to welcome him—they would be bound and handed to the local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Bo urged Zhai to parade his full ceremonial guard, gather the tribesmen outside the camp gate, and rebuke them: the Son of Heaven's chief minister had arrived, yet they had not all come far to welcome him—they would be bound and handed over to the local magistrates.

sentences.zh: 諸番羅拜請罪，乃稍賚其先至者，余皆懼不復來。

translations.literal: The tribesmen prostrated themselves and begged forgiveness; he then gave modest rewards only to those who had come first, and the rest, in fear, did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen prostrated themselves and pleaded for mercy; he then gave modest rewards only to those who had come first, and the rest, terrified, did not come again.

sentences.zh: 鑾還，薦博可屬大事。

translations.literal: When Zhai returned, he recommended Bo as fit to be entrusted with great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Zhai recommended Bo as someone fit to be entrusted with weighty affairs.

sentences.zh: 吉囊、俺答歲盜邊，尚書張瓚一切倚辦博。

translations.literal: Ginggang and Altan raided the borders yearly; Minister Zhang Zan relied on Bo for everything.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Ginggang and Altan raided the frontier, and Minister Zhang Zan relied on Bo for everything.

sentences.zh: 帝或中夜降手詔，博隨事條答，悉稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor would sometimes issue handwritten edicts in the middle of the night; Bo answered each point in order, and all accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would sometimes send handwritten edicts in the middle of the night; Bo answered each matter point by point, and every reply pleased him.

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫代瓚，博當遷，特奏留之。

translations.literal: When Mao Bowen replaced Zhang Zan, Bo was due for transfer, but the emperor specially ordered that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Bowen succeeded Zhang Zan, Bo was due for promotion elsewhere, but the emperor specially ordered that he be kept on.

sentences.zh: 已，遷山東提學副使，轉督糧參政。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be Vice Commissioner of Education in Shandong, then became Grain Transport Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as Vice Commissioner of Education in Shandong, and then became Grain Transport Administrative Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，超拜右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was promoted by special appointment to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546), he was promoted by special appointment to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 大興屯利，請募民墾田，永不征租。

translations.literal: Field colonies in Daxing were profitable; he requested that settlers be recruited to reclaim land with rent forever waived.
translations.idiomatic: The military colonies at Daxing were profitable; he asked that civilians be recruited to open new fields there, with rent waived forever.

sentences.zh: 又以暇修築肅州榆樹泉及甘州平川境外大蘆泉諸處墩臺，鑿龍首諸渠。

translations.literal: In his spare time he also repaired beacon towers at Yushuquan in Suzhou and Daluquan beyond the border at Pingchuan in Ganzhou, and opened irrigation canals at Longshou and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When he had leisure he also repaired beacon towers at Yushuquan in Suzhou and at Daluquan beyond the border at Pingchuan in Ganzhou, and opened irrigation canals at Longshou and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 初，罕東屬番避土魯番亂，遷肅州境上，時與居民戕殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, dependent tribes of Handom had fled Turfan disorder and moved to the borders of Suzhou, where they often fought and killed the local people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, dependent tribes of Handom had fled the turmoil in Turfan and moved onto the borders of Suzhou, where they often clashed with and killed local residents.

sentences.zh: 監生李時旸以為言，事下守臣。

translations.literal: Supervising student Li Shiyang reported this; the matter was referred to the guarding officials.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising student Li Shiyang brought the matter to attention, and it was referred to the local guarding officials.

sentences.zh: 博為築金塔、白城七堡，召其長，令率屬徙居之。

translations.literal: Bo built seven forts at Jinta and Baicheng, summoned their chiefs, and ordered them to lead their dependents to move there.
translations.idiomatic: Bo built seven forts at Jinta and Baicheng, summoned their chiefs, and ordered them to lead their people to relocate there.

sentences.zh: 諸番徙七百余帳，州境為之肅清。

translations.literal: More than seven hundred tents of tribesmen relocated, and the prefecture was thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: More than seven hundred tribal households moved, and the prefecture was thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 總兵官王繼祖卻寇永昌，鎮羌參將蔡勛等戰鎮番、山丹，三告捷，斬首百四十余級。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Wang Jizu repelled invaders at Yongchang; Deputy Regional Commander Cai Xun and others fought at Zhenfan and Shandan and thrice reported victory, beheading more than 140.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Wang Jizu drove the raiders from Yongchang; Deputy Regional Commander Cai Xun and others fought at Zhenfan and Shandan, reported victory three times, and took more than 140 heads.

sentences.zh: 進博右副都御史。

translations.literal: Bo was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞鎮甘肅，總督曾銑劾之，詔逮治。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan was stationed in Gansu; Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian impeached him, and an edict ordered his arrest.
translations.idiomatic: While Qiu Luan held command in Gansu, Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian impeached him, and an edict ordered his arrest and trial.

sentences.zh: 博亦發其貪罔三十事。

translations.literal: Bo also exposed thirty counts of his greed and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also exposed thirty charges of his greed and deceit.

sentences.zh: 鸞拜大將軍，數毀之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: When Qiu was appointed Grand General, he repeatedly slandered Bo, but the emperor would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiu was appointed Grand General, he repeatedly slandered Bo, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 服闋，鸞已誅，召拜兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, Qiu had already been executed; Bo was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, Qiu had already been executed; Bo was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 轉左，經略薊州、保定。

translations.literal: Transferred to the left post, he took charge of military affairs in Jizhou and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the left vice ministership and took charge of military affairs in Jizhou and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 初，俺答薄都城，由潮河川入，議者爭請為備。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Altan threatened the capital and entered through the Chaohé River valley, advocates all urged preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Altan threatened the capital and entered by the Chaohé River valley, officials all clamored for defenses to be prepared.

sentences.zh: 水湍悍，不可城。

translations.literal: The water was swift and fierce; walls could not be built.
translations.idiomatic: The current was too swift and violent to build walls along it.

sentences.zh: 博緣水勢建石墩，置戍守，還督京城九門。

translations.literal: Bo followed the water's course to erect stone blockhouses and posted garrisons; he also supervised the Nine Gates of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bo followed the water's course to build stone blockhouses, stationed guards there, and also supervised the capital's Nine Gates.

sentences.zh: 時因寇警，歲七月分兵守陴。

translations.literal: Because of the alarm of raids, each year in the seventh month troops were assigned to man the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the threat of raids, every year in the seventh month troops were assigned to man the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 博曰：「寇至，須鎮靜，奈何先事自擾？」

translations.literal: Bo said: "When the enemy comes, one must remain calm—why disturb ourselves beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: Bo said, "When the enemy comes, we must keep our composure—why throw ourselves into turmoil before anything has happened?"

sentences.zh: 罷其令。

translations.literal: The order was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The order was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 尋遷總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 博以薊逼京師，護畿甸陵寢為大，分布諸將，畫地為防。

translations.literal: Bo held that since Ji lay close to the capital, protecting the metropolitan district and imperial tombs was paramount; he assigned the various commanders and demarcated zones of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bo held that because Ji lay hard against the capital, the chief task was to protect the metropolitan district and the imperial tombs; he deployed the various commanders and divided the territory into defensive zones.

sentences.zh: 三十三年秋，把都兒及打來孫十余萬騎犯薊鎮，攻墻。

translations.literal: In autumn of the thirty-third year, Batu and Taisun with more than 100,000 horsemen invaded Jizhen and assaulted the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirty-third year (1554), Batu and Taisun led more than a hundred thousand horsemen against Jizhen and attacked the wall.

sentences.zh: 帝憂甚，數遣騎偵博。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply worried and repeatedly sent riders to scout Bo's situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply anxious and repeatedly sent riders to learn how Bo was faring.

sentences.zh: 博擐甲宿古北口城上，督總兵官周益昌等力禦。

translations.literal: Bo donned armor and slept on the walls of Gubeikou, urging Regional Commander Zhou Yichang and others to resist with all their might.
translations.idiomatic: Bo donned armor and slept on the walls of Gubeikou, pressing Regional Commander Zhou Yichang and the others to defend with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，馳賜緋豸衣，犒軍萬金。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and swiftly bestowed a crimson unicorn robe and rewarded the army with ten thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and at once sent him a crimson unicorn robe and rewarded the army with ten thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 寇攻四晝夜不得入，乃並攻孤山口，登墻。

translations.literal: The raiders attacked for four days and nights without entering, then together assaulted Gushankou and scaled the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders attacked for four days and nights without breaking in, then turned together on Gushankou and scaled the wall.

sentences.zh: 官軍斷一人腕，乃退屯虎頭山。

translations.literal: The government troops severed one man's wrist, and they withdrew to encamp at Hutou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops cut off one man's wrist, whereupon the raiders withdrew and encamped on Hutou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 博募死士，夜以火驚其營，寇擾亂，比明悉去。

translations.literal: Bo recruited daredevils who by night set fires to startle their camp; the raiders fell into confusion, and by dawn all had left.
translations.idiomatic: Bo recruited daredevils who by night set fires to panic the enemy camp; the raiders fell into disorder, and by dawn all had gone.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史，蔭子錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief; his son received the hereditary office of a battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, and his son was granted the hereditary rank of battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，打來孫復入益昌，擊卻之。

translations.literal: The next year Taisun again invaded Yichang and was beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Taisun again invaded Yichang, and Bo drove him back.

sentences.zh: 遂擢博兵部尚書，錄防秋功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Bo was then elevated to Minister of War; his autumn defense merit was recorded, and he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was then promoted to Minister of War; his merit in the autumn defense was recorded, and he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩父子招權利，諸司為所撓，博一切格不行。

translations.literal: Yan Song and his son monopolized power for profit; every office was obstructed by them, but Bo blocked everything they proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and his son used their power for profit, and every office was subject to their interference, but Bo blocked every request they made.

sentences.zh: 嵩恨博，會丁父憂去。

translations.literal: Yan hated Bo; when Bo happened to take leave for his father's death, [he was away].
translations.idiomatic: Yan resented Bo, and when Bo happened to leave office upon his father's death, [Yan seized the chance].

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書許論罷，帝起博代之。

translations.literal: When Minister Xu Lun was dismissed, the emperor recalled Bo to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Xu Lun was dismissed, the emperor recalled Bo to replace him.

sentences.zh: 博未終喪，疏辭。

translations.literal: Bo had not completed mourning and submitted a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had not yet completed his mourning period and submitted a memorial declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 而帝以大同右衛圍急，改博總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: But as Datong Right Guard was urgently besieged, the emperor changed Bo's assignment to Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: But because Datong Right Guard was in urgent peril, the emperor reassigned Bo as Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 博墨缞馳出關。

translations.literal: Bo went out through the pass dressed in mourning ink and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Still in mourning dress, Bo raced out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 未至，侍郎江東等以大軍進，寇引去。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Vice Minister Jiang Dong and others advanced with a great army, and the raiders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Vice Minister Jiang Dong and others advanced with a large army, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時右衛圍六月，守將王德戰亡，城中芻粟且盡，士死守無二心。

translations.literal: The Right Guard had been besieged six months; defending commander Wang De died in battle; fodder and grain in the city were nearly gone, yet the troops held fast with undivided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Guard had been besieged for six months; the defending commander Wang De had died in battle; fodder and grain in the city were nearly exhausted, yet the soldiers held on with undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 博厚撫恤，奏行善後十事。

translations.literal: Bo treated them generously and presented ten measures for post-incident relief.
translations.idiomatic: Bo treated them generously and memorialized ten measures for recovery after the siege.

sentences.zh: 以給事中張學顏言，留博鎮撫。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Supervising Secretary Zhang Xueyan, Bo was kept to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: On the urging of Supervising Secretary Zhang Xueyan, Bo was kept on to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲被寇租，因僉其丁壯為義勇，分隸諸將。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit rents in raided areas and enlisted able-bodied men as volunteer militia assigned to various commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to remit taxes in the raided districts and enrolled able-bodied men as volunteer militia, assigning them to the various commanders.

sentences.zh: 博以邊人不習車戰，寇入輒不支，請造箱車百輛，有警則右衛車東，左衛車西，使相聲援。

translations.literal: Bo said border people were unused to chariot warfare; whenever raiders entered they could not hold. He requested a hundred box wagons so that in an alarm the Right Guard wagons would go east and the Left Guard wagons west, giving mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Bo said the border troops were unused to chariot warfare and could not hold when raiders entered; he asked that a hundred box wagons be built so that in an alarm the wagons of the Right Guard would move east and those of the Left Guard west, giving one another support.

sentences.zh: 又以大同墻圮，繕治為急；

translations.literal: He also held that because the Datong wall was ruined, repairs were urgent;
translations.idiomatic: He also held that because the Datong wall had collapsed, repairs were the urgent priority;

sentences.zh: 次則塞銀釵、驛馬諸嶺，以絕窺紫荊路；

translations.literal: next, to block the passes at Yinchai, Yima, and the rest, to cut off the route toward Zijing;
translations.idiomatic: next, to block the passes at Yinchai, Yima, and elsewhere, to shut off the route toward Zijing;

sentences.zh: 備居庸南山，以絕窺陵寢畿甸路；

translations.literal: to prepare the southern slopes of Juyong, to cut off the route toward the tombs and the metropolitan district;
translations.idiomatic: to fortify the southern slopes of Juyong, to block the route toward the imperial tombs and the capital district;

sentences.zh: 修陽神地諸墻塹，以絕入山西路。

translations.literal: and to repair the walls and ditches at Yangshendi and elsewhere, to cut off the route into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: and to repair the walls and ditches at Yangshendi and elsewhere, to block the route into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乃於大同牛心山諸處築堡九，墩臺九十二，接左衛高山站，以達鎮城。

translations.literal: He then built nine forts at Niuxinshan in Datong and elsewhere, ninety-two beacon towers, linking the Gaoshan station of the Left Guard to reach the garrison city.
translations.idiomatic: He then built nine forts at Niuxinshan in Datong and elsewhere, along with ninety-two beacon towers, linking the Gaoshan station of the Left Guard to the garrison city.

sentences.zh: 浚大濠二，各十八里，小濠六十有四。

translations.literal: He dug two great moats, each eighteen li long, and sixty-four smaller moats.
translations.idiomatic: He dug two great moats, each eighteen li long, and sixty-four smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 五旬訖功，賜敕獎賚。

translations.literal: The work was finished in fifty days, and an edict of commendation and reward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The work was completed in fifty days, and the emperor issued an edict of commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 帝數欲召博還，又虞邊，以問嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly wished to recall Bo, yet also feared for the border, and asked Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly wished to recall Bo, yet also worried about the frontier, and consulted Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩雅不喜博，請令江東署部事，俟秋防畢徐議之，遂不召。

translations.literal: Yan had always disliked Bo; he asked that Jiang Dong be left to handle ministry affairs and that recall be discussed slowly after the autumn defense ended—so Bo was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had never liked Bo; he asked that Jiang Dong be left in charge at the ministry and that recall be discussed only after the autumn defense was over—so Bo was not summoned.

sentences.zh: 秋防訖，加太子太保，留鎮如故。

translations.literal: When the autumn defense ended, he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and remained on station as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the autumn defense ended, he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and remained at his post as before.

sentences.zh: 哱素把伶及叛人了都記等數以輕騎寇邊，博先後計擒之。

translations.literal: Bosala and the renegade Duduji and others repeatedly raided the border with light cavalry; Bo captured them by stratagem in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Bosala and the renegade Duduji and others repeatedly raided the border with light cavalry; Bo captured them one after another by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 又數出奇兵襲寇，寇稍徙帳。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly sent surprise forces to strike the raiders, and they gradually moved their camps away.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly sent surprise detachments against the raiders, who gradually moved their camps farther off.

sentences.zh: 因議築故總督翁萬達所創邊墻，招還內地民為寇掠者千六百余人。

translations.literal: He then proposed rebuilding the border wall created by the former Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda and brought back more than 1,600 inland people who had been carried off by raiders.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed rebuilding the border wall that former Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda had created and brought back more than sixteen hundred inland people who had been seized by raiders.

sentences.zh: 又請通宣、大荒田水利，薄其租。

translations.literal: He also asked to open irrigation for wasteland in Xuan and Da and to reduce the rent.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to open irrigation on wasteland in Xuanfu and Datong and to lighten the rent.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 改薊遼總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Grand Coordinator of Ji and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Ji and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 秋防竣，廷議欲召博還，吏部尚書吳鵬不可。

translations.literal: When the autumn defense ended, the court debated recalling Bo, but Minister of Personnel Wu Peng objected.
translations.idiomatic: When the autumn defense ended, the court debated recalling Bo, but Minister of Personnel Wu Peng would not agree.

sentences.zh: 鄭曉署兵部，爭之曰：「博在薊、遼則薊、遼安，在本兵則九邊俱安。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xiao, acting at the Ministry of War, argued: "If Bo is in Ji and Liaodong, Ji and Liaodong are secure; if he is at the central ministry, all Nine Frontier Circuits are secure."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiao, acting Minister of War, argued: "With Bo in Ji and Liaodong, Ji and Liaodong are secure; with him at the central ministry, all Nine Frontier Circuits are secure."

sentences.zh: 乃如還，加少保。

translations.literal: He was then recalled and given the additional title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled and given the additional title of Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 帝憂邊甚，博每先事為防，帝眷倚若左右手。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply anxious about the border; Bo always prepared defenses beforehand, and the emperor relied on him as on his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply anxious about the frontier; Bo always prepared defenses before trouble arose, and the emperor relied on him as on his own two hands.

sentences.zh: 嘗語閣臣：「自博入，朕每憂邊，其語博預為謀。」

translations.literal: He once told the Grand Secretaries: "Since Bo entered office, whenever I worry about the border, I speak with Bo and plan ahead."
translations.idiomatic: He once told the Grand Secretaries, "Since Bo took office, whenever I worry about the frontier, I speak with Bo and plan ahead."

sentences.zh: 博上言：「今九邊，薊鎮為重。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized: "Of the Nine Frontier Circuits today, Jizhen is the weightiest.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized, "Of the Nine Frontier Circuits today, Jizhen is the most critical.

sentences.zh: 請敕邊臣逐大同寇，使不得近薊，宣、大諸將從獨石偵情形，預備黃花、古北諸要害，使一騎不得入關，即首功也。」

translations.literal: I ask that frontier officials be ordered to drive off Datong raiders so they cannot approach Ji; generals in Xuan and Da should scout from Dushi; and key points such as Huanghua and Gubei should be prepared so that not a single horseman enters the pass—that alone would count as the highest merit."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that frontier officials be ordered to drive off the Datong raiders so they cannot approach Ji; the generals in Xuanfu and Datong should scout from Dushi; and key points such as Huanghua and Gubei should be prepared so that not a single horseman enters the pass—that alone would be the highest merit."

sentences.zh: 帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四十二年十月，寇擁眾窺薊州，聲言犯遼陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-second year, raiders massed and watched Jizhou, proclaiming that they would strike Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-second year (1563), the raiders gathered in force and probed Jizhou, claiming they would attack Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 總督楊選帥師東，博檄止之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Yang Xuan led his army east; Bo sent orders to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yang Xuan led his army eastward; Bo sent orders to halt him.

sentences.zh: 又手書三往，卒不從。

translations.literal: He also wrote three personal letters, but in the end Yang would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote three personal letters in succession, but Yang still would not obey.

sentences.zh: 博拊幾曰：「敗矣。」

translations.literal: Bo struck the table and said: "We are defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Bo struck the table and said, "We are lost."

sentences.zh: 急征兵入援，寇已潰墻子嶺，犯通州。

translations.literal: He urgently levied troops to reinforce, but the raiders had already broken through at Qiangziling and invaded Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently levied troops to reinforce the capital, but the raiders had already broken through at Qiangziling and invaded Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「庚戌事又見矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "The events of gengxu are upon us again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "The disaster of the gengxu year has come again."

sentences.zh: 諸路兵先後至。

translations.literal: Troops from the various routes arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the various routes arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 命宣大總督江東統文武大臣分守皇城、京城，鎮遠侯顧寰以京營兵分布城內外。

translations.literal: He ordered Grand Coordinator Jiang Dong of Xuan and Da to lead civil and military officials in guarding the Imperial City and the capital, and Marquis Gu Huan of Zhenyuan to deploy capital-garrison troops inside and outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand Coordinator Jiang Dong of Xuanfu and Datong to lead civil and military officials in guarding the Imperial City and the capital, while Marquis Gu Huan of Zhenyuan deployed capital-garrison troops throughout the city inside and out.

sentences.zh: 寇解而東，躪順義、三河，飽掠去。

translations.literal: The raiders broke off and went east, trampling Shunyi and Sanhe, and left after sating themselves with plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders broke away and marched east, overrunning Shunyi and Sanhe before departing, sated with plunder.

sentences.zh: 援兵不發一矢，取道斃及零騎傷殘者報首功。

translations.literal: The relief troops did not shoot a single arrow; they took corpses along the road and scattered wounded horsemen and reported them as merit in heads.
translations.idiomatic: The relief forces never loosed a single arrow; they collected corpses along the roads and the odd wounded rider and reported them as victories.

sentences.zh: 帝怏怏，諭博曰：「賊復飽飏，何以懲後？」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and told Bo: "The bandits have again feasted and fled—how are later offenders to be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased and said to Bo, "The raiders have feasted on our lands and ridden off again—how will we deter those who come after?"

sentences.zh: 遂誅選。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan was then executed.

sentences.zh: 博懼及，徐階力保持之。

translations.literal: Bo feared he would be implicated; Xu Jie strongly intervened to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo feared he would be implicated as well; Xu Jie intervened forcefully on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝念博前功，不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of Bo's earlier merit, did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Bo's earlier service, the emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 久之，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to be Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，請遵遺詔，錄建言諸臣，死者皆贈恤。

translations.literal: When the Longqing reign began, he asked that the late emperor's testament be followed, that officials who had offered remonstrance be recorded, and that the dead all receive posthumous honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, he asked that the late emperor's testament be followed, that officials who had remonstrated be recorded, and that the dead among them all receive posthumous honors and relief.

sentences.zh: 時方計群吏，山西人無一被黜者。

translations.literal: At the time officials were being evaluated; not a single man from Shanxi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officials were being evaluated for retention or dismissal, and not a single man from Shanxi was removed.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡應嘉劾博庇其鄉人，博連疏乞休。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hu Yingjia impeached Bo for shielding his fellow provincials; Bo submitted repeated memorials asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hu Yingjia impeached Bo for favoring his fellow provincials; Bo submitted repeated memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 並慰留，且斥言者。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and kept him on, and also rebuked the accusers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and kept him in office, and also rebuked his accusers.

sentences.zh: 一品滿三考，進少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When he completed three evaluations at the first rank, he was advanced to Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When he completed three evaluations at the first rank, he was promoted to Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝將遊南海子，博率同列諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to tour the Southern Park, Bo led his colleagues in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to tour the Southern Park, Bo led his colleagues in remonstrating against it.

sentences.zh: 御史詹仰庇以直言罷，博爭之。

translations.literal: Censor Zhan Yangbi was dismissed for outspoken remonstrance; Bo argued on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhan Yangbi was dismissed for speaking out plainly; Bo argued forcefully on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 屯鹽都御史龐尚鵬被論，博議留。

translations.literal: Salt-field Censor Pang Shangpeng was impeached; Bo argued that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-field Censor Pang Shangpeng came under attack; Bo argued that he should be kept on.

sentences.zh: 懺旨，遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: He regretted having displeased the emperor and then resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Regretting that he had displeased the emperor, he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉體乾等交章乞留，不聽。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Tigan and others submitted joint memorials asking that he be kept, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Tigan and others submitted joint memorials asking that he be retained, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱掌吏部，薦博堪本兵。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gong was acting at the Ministry of Personnel and recommended Bo as fit for the central military ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gong, acting at the Ministry of Personnel, recommended Bo as fit to head the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 詔以吏部尚書理兵部事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to handle Ministry of War affairs as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to handle Ministry of War affairs while retaining his post as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 陳薊、昌戰守方略，謂：「議者以守墻為怯，言可聽，實無少效。

translations.literal: He set forth strategies for fighting and defending in Ji and Chang, saying: "Those who debate call wall defense cowardly; their words sound plausible, but in fact they achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth strategies for fighting and defending in Ji and Changping, saying, "Debaters call wall defense cowardly; their words sound plausible, but in fact they achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 墻外邀擊，害七利三；

translations.literal: Striking outside the wall brings seven harms and three benefits;
translations.idiomatic: Striking outside the wall brings seven harms against three benefits;

sentences.zh: 墻內格鬥，利一害九。

translations.literal: fighting inside the wall brings one benefit and nine harms.
translations.idiomatic: fighting inside the wall brings one benefit against nine harms.

sentences.zh: 夫因墻守，所謂先處戰地而待敵。

translations.literal: To defend by relying on the wall is what is called taking the battlefield first and awaiting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: To defend by relying on the wall is what is called taking the battlefield first and awaiting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 名守，實戰也。

translations.literal: It is called defense, but in fact it is combat.
translations.idiomatic: It is called defense, but in truth it is combat.

sentences.zh: 臣為總督，嘗拒打來孫十萬眾，以為當守墻無疑。」

translations.literal: When I was Grand Coordinator, I once repelled a hundred thousand of Taisun's horde and hold that wall defense is beyond doubt."
translations.idiomatic: When I served as Grand Coordinator, I once repelled a hundred thousand of Taisun's horde, and I hold that wall defense is beyond question."

sentences.zh: 因陳明應援、申駐守、處京營、諭屬夷、修內治諸事，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: He then set forth matters of timely reinforcement, strengthened garrison duty, disposition of the capital army, instruction of dependent tribes, and repair of internal governance; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth matters of timely reinforcement, strengthened garrison duty, disposition of the capital army, instruction of dependent tribes, and repair of internal governance; the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 博魁梧豐碩，臨事安閑有識量。

translations.literal: Bo was tall and stout; in affairs he was calm and possessed discernment and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was tall and powerfully built; in affairs he was calm and possessed discernment and breadth of view.

sentences.zh: 出入中外四十余年，始終以兵事著。

translations.literal: For more than forty years moving between court and frontier, he was known throughout for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years moving between court and frontier, he was known throughout for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，高拱罷，乃改博吏部，進少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Gao Gong was dismissed, Bo was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and advanced to Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Gao Gong was dismissed, Bo was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，疾作，三疏乞致仕歸。

translations.literal: The next autumn illness set in; he submitted three memorials asking to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he fell ill and submitted three memorials asking to retire and return home.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: A year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor and the posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 拱柄國時，欲中徐階危禍，博造拱，力為解。

translations.literal: When Gao held power, he wished to entrap Xu Jie in disaster; Bo visited Gao and worked hard to explain matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao held power, he wished to entrap Xu Jie in ruin; Bo visited Gao and worked hard to clear the matter.

sentences.zh: 拱亦心動，事獲已。

translations.literal: Gao's heart was also moved, and the affair was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was moved as well, and the affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其後張居正逐拱，將周內其罪，博毅然爭之。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhang Juzheng drove Gao out and was about to weave a full indictment of his crimes, Bo argued against it resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Juzheng drove Gao out and was about to weave a full indictment of his crimes, Bo argued against it with firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 及興王大臣獄，博與都御史葛守禮詣居正力為解。

translations.literal: When the case of the Xingwang ministers arose, Bo and Censor-in-Chief Ge Shouli went to Zhang Juzheng and worked hard to obtain a resolution.
translations.idiomatic: When the case of the Xingwang ministers arose, Bo and Censor-in-Chief Ge Shouli went to Zhang Juzheng and worked hard to obtain a resolution.

sentences.zh: 居正憤曰：「二公謂我甘心高公耶？」

translations.literal: Zhang said angrily: "Do you two gentlemen think I am bent on destroying Lord Gao?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said angrily, "Do you two gentlemen think I am bent on destroying Lord Gao?"

sentences.zh: 博曰：「非敢然也，然非公不能回天。」

translations.literal: Bo said: "We dare not think so, yet without you, sir, heaven cannot be turned back."
translations.idiomatic: Bo said, "We dare not think so, yet without you, sir, heaven itself cannot be turned back."

sentences.zh: 會帝命守禮偕都督朱希孝會訊，博陰為畫計，使校尉怵大臣改供；

translations.literal: When the emperor ordered Shouli together with Regional Commander Zhu Xixiao to conduct a joint inquiry, Bo secretly devised a plan so that guards intimidated the ministers into changing their testimony;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered Shouli together with Regional Commander Zhu Xixiao to conduct a joint inquiry, Bo secretly devised a plan by which guards intimidated the ministers into changing their testimony;

sentences.zh: 又令拱仆雜稠人中，令大臣識別，茫然莫辨，事乃白。

translations.literal: he also had Gao's servants mixed among the crowd and told the ministers to identify them; they could not tell them apart in confusion, and the affair was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: he also had Gao's servants mixed among the crowd and told the ministers to identify them; in the confusion they could tell nothing apart, and the affair was cleared.

sentences.zh: 人以是稱博長者。

translations.literal: People therefore praised Bo as a man of mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: People therefore praised Bo as a man of mature and generous character.

sentences.zh: 子俊民，字伯章，嘉靖四十一年進士。

translations.literal: His son Junmin, styled Bozhang, passed the jinshi in the forty-first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junmin, styled Bozhang, passed the jinshi examinations in the forty-first year of Jiajing (1562).

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事，歷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to become a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，遷河南提學副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was transferred to be Vice Commissioner of Education in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was transferred to serve as Vice Commissioner of Education in Henan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，歷太僕少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he rose to Junior Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he rose to Junior Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 父博致政，侍歸。

translations.literal: When his father Bo retired, he attended him home.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Bo retired from office, he went home to attend him.

sentences.zh: 起故官，累遷兵部左侍郎署部事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to his former post and was promoted in succession to Left Vice Minister of War, acting at the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former post and was promoted in succession to Left Vice Minister of War, acting head of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 時議撦力克嗣封。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over whether Tümen's descendant Ligdan should succeed to a hereditary title.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated whether Ligdan, descendant of Tümen, should succeed to a hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 俊民言：「款未可遽罷。

translations.literal: Junmin said: "The peace agreement cannot be abruptly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Junmin said, "The peace agreement cannot be abruptly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 惟內修守備，而外勒西部，使盡還巢，申定市額，使無濫索而已。」

translations.literal: We need only strengthen defenses within and press the western tribes without, make them all return to their camps, fix market quotas, and prevent excessive demands—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: We need only strengthen our defenses within and press the western tribes from without, make them all return to their camps, fix market quotas, and prevent excessive demands—that is all."

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The debate was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was then settled.

sentences.zh: 進戶部尚書，總督倉場。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Revenue and Grand Coordinator of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue and appointed Grand Coordinator of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 十九年，還理部事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he returned to handle ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he returned to handle affairs at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 河南大饑，人相食，請發銀米各數十萬。

translations.literal: Henan suffered great famine and people ate one another; he asked that several hundred thousand taels of silver and piculs of grain be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Henan suffered a great famine in which people ate one another; he asked that several hundred thousand taels of silver and piculs of grain be issued.

sentences.zh: 或議其稽緩，因自劾求罷。

translations.literal: Some criticized his delay; he therefore impeached himself and asked to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Some criticized his delay; he therefore impeached himself and asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 疏六上，不允。

translations.literal: He submitted six memorials; none was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted six memorials; none was granted.

sentences.zh: 小人競請開礦，俊民爭不得，稅使乃四出。

translations.literal: Petty men competed to ask that mines be opened; Junmin could not prevail in argument, and tax commissioners were then sent out in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men competed to ask that mines be opened; Junmin could not prevail in argument, and tax commissioners were then dispatched in all directions.

sentences.zh: 天下騷然，時以咎俊民。

translations.literal: The empire was in uproar, and at the time blame was laid on Junmin.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was thrown into turmoil, and at the time the blame was laid on Junmin.

sentences.zh: 在事歷三考，累加太子太保。

translations.literal: In office he passed three evaluations and was repeatedly given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In office he passed three evaluations and was repeatedly given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈少保。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 後敘東征轉餉功，贈少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later, when merit in transporting supplies for the eastern campaign was recorded, he was posthumously given Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merit in transporting supplies for the eastern campaign was recorded, he was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 馬森，字孔養，懷安人。

translations.literal: Ma Sen, styled Kongyang, was a man of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sen, styled Kongyang, was a native of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 父俊，晚得子，家人抱之墜，殞焉。

translations.literal: His father Jun had a son late in life; a servant holding the child let him fall, and the child died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had a son late in life; a servant holding the child let him fall, and the child died.

sentences.zh: 俊紿其妻曰「我誤也」，不之罪。

translations.literal: Jun deceived his wife, saying "It was my fault," and did not punish anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Jun told his wife, "It was my fault," and did not punish anyone.

sentences.zh: 逾年而舉森。

translations.literal: A year later Sen was born.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Sen was born.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年成進士，授戶部主事，歷太平知府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as prefect of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing (1535) he passed the jinshi examinations, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and later served as prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 民有兄弟訟者，予鏡令照曰：「若二人老矣，忍傷天性乎？」

translations.literal: When brothers came to sue one another, he gave them a mirror and told them to look and said: "You two are already old—can you bear to wound your natural bond?"
translations.idiomatic: When brothers came to court against one another, he gave them a mirror and told them to look at themselves, saying, "You two are already old—can you bear to wound the bond of kinship?"

sentences.zh: 皆感泣謝去。

translations.literal: All wept in emotion and withdrew with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Both wept and withdrew with thanks.

sentences.zh: 再遷江西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to serve as Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 有進士嬖外婦而殺妻，撫按欲緩其獄，森卒抵之法。

translations.literal: A jinshi kept a concubine and killed his wife; the governor and surveillance commissioner wished to ease his case, but Sen in the end applied the law against him.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi kept a concubine and murdered his wife; the governor and surveillance commissioner wished to ease his case, but Sen in the end had him punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 歷左布政使，就擢巡撫右副都御史。

translations.literal: He rose to be Left Administrative Commissioner and was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Left Administrative Commissioner and was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部右侍郎，改戶部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Justice and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Justice and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，森在江西薦布政使宋淳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sen was in Jiangxi, he had recommended Administrative Commissioner Song Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sen was in Jiangxi, he had recommended Administrative Commissioner Song Chun.

sentences.zh: 淳後撫南、贛，以贓敗，森坐調大理卿。

translations.literal: Song later governed Nan and Gan and was ruined by corruption; Sen was implicated and transferred to be chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Song later governed Nan and Gan and was ruined by corruption; Sen was implicated and transferred to serve as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 屢駁疑獄，與刑部尚書鄭曉、都御史周延稱為「三平」。

translations.literal: He repeatedly overturned doubtful cases and, with Minister of Justice Zheng Xiao and Censor-in-Chief Zhou Yan, was called the "Three Fair Ones."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly overturned doubtful cases and, together with Minister of Justice Zheng Xiao and Censor-in-Chief Zhou Yan, was known as one of the "Three Fair Ones."

sentences.zh: 病歸，起南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He returned home on grounds of illness, then was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home on grounds of illness, then was recalled to serve as Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 改戶部，督倉場，尋轉左。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, supervised the granary depots, and soon moved to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, supervised the granary depots, and soon moved to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 以右都御史總督漕運，兼巡撫鳳陽，遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: As Right Censor-in-Chief he was Grand Coordinator of the grain transport and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Fengyang, then was transferred to be Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Censor-in-Chief he served as Grand Coordinator of the grain transport and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Fengyang, then was appointed Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，改北部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was transferred to the northern ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was transferred to the northern ministry in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 是時，登極詔書蠲天下田租半。

translations.literal: At that time the accession edict remitted half the land tax throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the accession edict remitted half the land tax throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 太倉歲入少，不能副經費，而京、通二倉積貯無幾。

translations.literal: Annual receipts into the Taicang granary were small and could not meet expenditures, while the Beijing and Tongzhou depots had little in store.
translations.idiomatic: Annual receipts into the Taicang granary were small and could not meet expenditures, while the Beijing and Tongzhou depots had little in store.

sentences.zh: 森鉤校搜剔，條行十余事。

translations.literal: Sen audited accounts minutely and set forth more than ten measures in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Sen audited accounts minutely and set forth more than ten detailed measures.

sentences.zh: 又列上錢谷出入之數，勸帝節儉。

translations.literal: He also listed figures for revenue and expenditure and urged the emperor to practice frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He also listed figures for revenue and expenditure and urged the emperor to practice frugality.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔責令措置，森奏：「祖宗舊制，河、淮以南以四百萬供京師，河、淮以北以八百萬供邊。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a handwritten edict rebuking him and ordering remedies; Sen memorialized: "The ancestral system provided four million for the capital from south of the Yellow and Huai rivers, and eight million for the frontier from north of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a handwritten edict rebuking him and ordering remedies; Sen memorialized, "Under the ancestral system, four million piculs from south of the Yellow and Huai rivers supplied the capital, and eight million from the north supplied the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一歲之入，足供一歲之用。

translations.literal: One year's income was sufficient for one year's use.
translations.idiomatic: One year's income was sufficient for one year's expenses.

sentences.zh: 後邊陲多事，支費漸繁，一變而有客兵之年例，再變而有主兵之年例。

translations.literal: Later the frontier saw many troubles and expenditures gradually grew complex; one change brought the annual quota for guest troops, a second change brought the annual quota for regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later the frontier saw many troubles and expenditures gradually grew complex; one change brought the annual quota for guest troops, and a second brought the annual quota for regular troops.

sentences.zh: 其初止三五十萬耳，後漸增至二百三十余萬。

translations.literal: At first it was only three or five hundred thousand, but later it gradually rose to more than 2.3 million.
translations.idiomatic: At first it was only three or five hundred thousand, but later it gradually rose to more than 2.3 million.

sentences.zh: 屯田十虧七八，鹽法十折四五，民運十逋二三，悉以年例補之。

translations.literal: Military colonies lost seven or eight tenths, the salt monopoly was discounted four or five tenths, and civilian transport defaulted two or three tenths—all were made up from the annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Military colonies lost seven or eight tenths of their yield, the salt monopoly was discounted four or five tenths, and civilian transport defaulted two or three tenths—all were made up from the annual quota.

sentences.zh: 在邊則士馬不多於昔，在太倉則輸入不益於前，而所費數倍。

translations.literal: On the frontier there were no more soldiers and horses than before; into Taicang no more was delivered than before—yet expenditures were several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier there were no more soldiers and horses than before; into Taicang no more was delivered than before—yet expenditures were several times greater.

sentences.zh: 重以詔書蠲除，故今日告匱，視往歲有加。

translations.literal: Added to this was the remission in the edict, so today's shortage is greater than in past years.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this was the remission ordered in the edict, so today's shortage is greater than in past years.

sentences.zh: 臣前所區畫，算及錙銖，不過紓目前急，而於國之大體，民之元氣，未暇深慮。

translations.literal: What I planned before, reckoned to the last cash, only eased the present urgency; I had no leisure to think deeply about the great structure of the state or the vital strength of the people.
translations.idiomatic: What I planned before, reckoned to the last cash, only eased the present urgency; I had no leisure to think deeply about the great structure of the state or the vital strength of the people.

sentences.zh: 願廣集眾思，令廷臣各陳所見。」

translations.literal: I wish that many minds be gathered and court officials each set forth their views."
translations.idiomatic: I wish that many minds be gathered and that court officials each set forth their views."

sentences.zh: 又奏河東、四川、雲南、福建、廣東、靈州鹽課事宜。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on salt levies in Hedong, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Guangdong, and Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on salt levies in Hedong, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Guangdong, and Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔皆如所請。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all as he had requested.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命中官崔敏發戶部銀六萬市黃金。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered the eunuch Cui Min to take sixty thousand taels of silver from the Ministry of Revenue to buy gold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered the eunuch Cui Min to take sixty thousand taels of silver from the Ministry of Revenue to buy gold.

sentences.zh: 森持不可，且言，故事禦劄皆由內閣下，無司禮徑傳者，事乃止。

translations.literal: Sen held that it could not be done and also said that by precedent all imperial rescripts passed through the Grand Secretariat; none went directly from the Directorate of Ceremonial—and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sen held that it could not be done and also said that by precedent all imperial rescripts passed through the Grand Secretariat; none went directly from the Directorate of Ceremonial—and the matter was stopped.

sentences.zh: 即，又命購珠寶，森亦力爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Soon after, he was again ordered to purchase pearls and gems; Sen also argued forcefully, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was again ordered to purchase pearls and gems; Sen argued forcefully again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 三年，以母老乞終養。

translations.literal: In the third year, on grounds that his mother was old, he asked to retire and care for her to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on grounds that his mother was old, he asked to retire and care for her until the end.

sentences.zh: 賜馳驛歸，後屢薦不起。

translations.literal: He was granted post-horses for his return; later he was repeatedly recommended but would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted post-horses for his return home; later he was repeatedly recommended but would not take office again.

sentences.zh: 森為考官時，夏言婿出其門，欲介之見言，謝不往。

translations.literal: When Sen was an examiner, a son-in-law of Xia Yan had been his student and wished to introduce him to Yan; Sen declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Sen served as an examiner, a son-in-law of Xia Yan had been his student and wished to introduce him to Yan; Sen declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩聞而悅之，森亦不附。

translations.literal: Yan Song heard of this and was pleased with him, yet Sen also did not attach himself to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song heard of this and was pleased with him, yet Sen would not attach himself to Yan either.

sentences.zh: 為徐階所重，遂引用之。

translations.literal: He was valued by Xu Jie, who then brought him into office.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie valued him and brought him into office.

sentences.zh: 裏居，贊巡撫龐尚鵬行一條鞭法，鄉人為立報功祠。

translations.literal: Living at home, he praised Grand Coordinator Pang Shangpeng for implementing the single-whip method of taxation, and his fellow townsmen erected a shrine to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: At home in retirement, he praised Grand Coordinator Pang Shangpeng for implementing the single-whip method of taxation, and his fellow townsmen erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Wanli (1580).

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 劉體乾，字子元，東安人。

translations.literal: Liu Tigan, styled Ziyuan, was a man of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tigan, styled Ziyuan, was a native of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-third year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the twenty-third year of Jiajing (1544).

sentences.zh: 授行人，改兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a courier and transferred to be a supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier and transferred to serve as a supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監鮑忠卒，其黨李慶為其侄鮑恩等八人乞遷。

translations.literal: Eunuch-director Bao Zhong of the Directorate of Ceremonial died; his follower Li Qing asked transfers for his nephew Bao En and seven others.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch-director Bao Zhong of the Directorate of Ceremonial died; his follower Li Qing asked that transfers be granted to his nephew Bao En and seven others.

sentences.zh: 帝已許之，以體乾言，止錄三人。

translations.literal: The emperor had already agreed, but on Tigan's word only three were recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already agreed, but on Tigan's urging only three were approved.

sentences.zh: 轉左給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a left supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as a left supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝以財用絀，詔廷臣集議。

translations.literal: Because finances were strained, the emperor ordered court officials to gather for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Because state finances were strained, the emperor ordered court officials to gather for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 多請追宿逋，增賦額。

translations.literal: Most asked to pursue old arrears and increase tax quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Most asked to pursue old arrears and increase tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 體乾獨上奏曰：「蘇軾有言：『豐財之道，惟在去其害財者。』

translations.literal: Tigan alone memorialized: "Su Shi said: 'The way to enrich the treasury is only to remove what harms the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan alone memorialized, "Su Shi said, 'The way to enrich the treasury is only to remove what harms the treasury.

sentences.zh: 今之害最大者有二，冗吏、冗費是也。

translations.literal: Today the greatest harms are two: redundant officials and redundant expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Today the greatest harms are two: redundant officials and redundant expenditures.

sentences.zh: 歷代官制，漢七千五百員，唐萬八千員，宋極冗至三萬四千員。

translations.literal: Official systems of successive dynasties: Han had 7,500 posts, Tang 18,000, and Song at its most redundant reached 34,000.
translations.idiomatic: Official systems of successive dynasties: Han had 7,500 posts, Tang 18,000, and Song at its most redundant reached 34,000.

sentences.zh: 本朝自成化五年，武職已逾八萬。

translations.literal: In our dynasty from the fifth year of Chenghua, military posts already exceeded 80,000.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, from the fifth year of Chenghua onward, military posts already exceeded 80,000.

sentences.zh: 合文職，蓋十萬余。

translations.literal: Together with civil posts, there are probably more than 100,000.
translations.idiomatic: Together with civil posts, there are probably more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 今邊功升授、勛貴傳請、曹局添設、大臣恩蔭，加以廠衛、監局、勇士、匠人之屬，歲增月益，不可悉舉。

translations.literal: Today promotions for frontier merit, requests from nobles, added bureaus, ministers' hereditary privileges, together with the Brocade Guard, supervisory offices, braves, artisans, and the like increase month by month and cannot all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: Today promotions for frontier merit, requests from nobles, added bureaus, ministers' hereditary privileges, together with the Embroidered Uniform Guard, supervisory offices, braves, artisans, and the like increase month by month and cannot all be listed.

sentences.zh: 多一官，則多一官之費。

translations.literal: One more official means one more official's expense.
translations.idiomatic: One more official means one more official's expense.

sentences.zh: 請嚴敕請曹，清革冗濫，減俸將不貲。

translations.literal: I ask that the various bureaus be strictly ordered to purge redundant and excessive appointments; reducing salaries will not be enough.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the various bureaus be strictly ordered to purge redundant and excessive appointments; reducing salaries alone will not suffice.

sentences.zh: 又聞光錄庫金，自嘉靖改元至十五年，積至八十萬。

translations.literal: I also hear that gold in the Guanglu Treasury from the Jiajing reign change to the fifteenth year accumulated to 800,000.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that gold in the Guanglu Treasury from the beginning of the Jiajing reign to the fifteenth year had accumulated to eight hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 自二十一年以後，供億日增，余藏頓盡。

translations.literal: From the twenty-first year onward, daily expenditures grew and the surplus was suddenly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: From the twenty-first year onward, daily expenditures grew and the surplus was suddenly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 進禦果蔬，初無定額，止示內監片紙，如數供禦。

translations.literal: Fruits and vegetables presented to the palace at first had no fixed quota; the inner eunuchs showed only a slip of paper and supplies were furnished as ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits and vegetables presented to the palace at first had no fixed quota; the inner eunuchs showed only a slip of paper and supplies were furnished as ordered.

sentences.zh: 乾沒狼籍，輒轉鬻市人。

translations.literal: They embezzled freely and promptly resold to market people.
translations.idiomatic: They embezzled freely and promptly resold the goods to merchants.

sentences.zh: 其他諸曹，侵盜尤多。

translations.literal: Other bureaus plundered even more.
translations.idiomatic: Other bureaus plundered even more.

sentences.zh: 宜著為令典，歲終使科道臣會計之，以清冗費。

translations.literal: This should be set down as statute; at year's end censorial officials should audit accounts to clear redundant expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: This should be set down as statute; at year's end censorial officials should audit accounts to clear redundant expenditures.

sentences.zh: 二冗既革，國計自裕。

translations.literal: Once the two redundancies are removed, state finances will naturally be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two redundancies are removed, state finances will naturally be ample.

sentences.zh: 舍是而督逋、增賦，是揚湯止沸也。」

translations.literal: To abandon this and instead pursue arrears and increase levies is to ladle boiling water to stop the pot from boiling over."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this and instead pursue arrears and increase levies is to ladle boiling water to stop the pot from boiling over."

sentences.zh: 於是部議請汰各監局人匠。

translations.literal: The ministry then deliberated and asked to reduce artisans in the various supervisory offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry then deliberated and asked to reduce artisans in the various supervisory offices.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 累官通政使，遷刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 改戶部左侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Coordinator of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Grand Coordinator of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，進南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was advanced to Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was promoted to Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 南畿、湖廣、江西銀布絹米積逋二百六十余萬，鳳陽園陵九衛官軍四萬，而倉粟無一月儲。

translations.literal: In the Southern Metropolitan Region, Huguang, and Jiangxi, arrears in silver, cloth, silk, and grain accumulated to more than 2.6 million; at the Fengyang imperial tombs nine guards had 40,000 troops, yet the depots had not a month's stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the Southern Metropolitan Region, Huguang, and Jiangxi, arrears in silver, cloth, silk, and grain accumulated to more than 2.6 million; at the Fengyang imperial tombs nine guards had forty thousand troops, yet the depots had not a month's stores.

sentences.zh: 體乾再疏請責成有司，又條上六事，皆報可。

translations.literal: Tigan again memorialized asking that local officials be held responsible and also set forth six measures in detail; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan again memorialized asking that local officials be held responsible and also set forth six measures in detail; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 馬森去，召改北部。

translations.literal: When Ma Sen left, Tigan was summoned to the northern ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sen left office, Tigan was summoned to the northern ministry in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 詔取太倉銀三十萬兩。

translations.literal: An edict ordered thirty thousand taels of silver taken from Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered three hundred thousand taels of silver taken from the Taicang granary treasury.

sentences.zh: 體乾言：「太倉銀所存三百七十萬耳，而九邊年例二百七十六萬有奇，在京軍糧商價百有余萬薊州、大同諸鎮例外奏乞不與焉。

translations.literal: Tigan said: "Only 3.7 million taels remain in Taicang, while the Nine Frontier Circuits' annual quota is more than 2.76 million, army grain and market prices in the capital exceed one million, not counting extraordinary requests from Jizhou, Datong, and other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan said, "Only 3.7 million taels remain in Taicang, while the Nine Frontier Circuits' annual quota is more than 2.76 million, army grain and market prices in the capital exceed one million—not counting extraordinary requests from Jizhou, Datong, and other garrisons.

sentences.zh: 若復取以上供，經費安辦？」

translations.literal: If more is taken for palace supply, how are regular expenditures to be met?"
translations.idiomatic: If more is taken for palace supply, how are regular expenditures to be met?"

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 體乾復奏：「今國計絀乏，大小臣工所共知。

translations.literal: Tigan memorialized again: "Today's state finances are strained—this is known to officials great and small.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan memorialized again, "Today's state finances are strained—this is known to officials great and small.

sentences.zh: 即存庫之數，乃近遣御史所搜括，明歲則無策矣。

translations.literal: Even the figures now in store were recently gathered by censors sent out; next year there will be no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Even the figures now in store were recently gathered by censors sent out; next year there will be no remedy.

sentences.zh: 今盡以供無益費，萬一變起倉卒，如國計何？」

translations.literal: To spend it all now on useless expenses—if sudden crisis arises, what of state finances?"
translations.idiomatic: To spend it all now on useless expenses—if sudden crisis arises, what will become of state finances?"

sentences.zh: 於是給事中李已、楊一魁、龍光，御史劉思問、蘇士潤、賀一桂，傅孟春交章乞如體乾言，閣臣李春芳等皆上疏請，乃命止進十萬兩。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Li Yi, Yang Yikui, and Long Guang, censors Liu Siwen, Su Shirun, He Yigui, and Fu Mengchun submitted joint memorials asking as Tigan said; Grand Secretaries Li Chunfang and others all memorialized—and the emperor ordered only 100,000 taels advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Li Yi, Yang Yikui, and Long Guang, censors Liu Siwen, Su Shirun, He Yigui, and Fu Mengchun submitted joint memorials supporting Tigan; Grand Secretaries Li Chunfang and others all memorialized as well—and the emperor ordered only one hundred thousand taels advanced.

sentences.zh: 又奏太和山香稅宜如泰山例，有司董之，毋屬內臣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that incense tax at Mount Taihe should follow the Mount Tai precedent, supervised by regular officials and not entrusted to inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the incense tax at Mount Taihe should follow the Mount Tai precedent, supervised by regular officials and not entrusted to inner eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，奪俸半年。

translations.literal: He offended the emperor's intent and had his salary suspended for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the emperor and had his salary suspended for half a year.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問九邊軍餉，太倉歲發及四方解納之數。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked about frontier army pay, annual disbursements from Taicang, and tribute delivered from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked about frontier army pay, annual disbursements from Taicang, and tribute delivered from the four directions.

sentences.zh: 體乾奏：「祖宗朝止遼東、大同、宣府、延綏四鎮，繼以寧夏、甘肅、薊州，又繼以固原、山西，今密雲、昌平、永平、易州俱列戍矣。

translations.literal: Tigan memorialized: "In the ancestral reign there were only the four garrisons of Liaodong, Datong, Xuanfu, and Yansui; then Ningxia and Gansu were added, then Jizhou, then Guyuan and Shanxi; today Miyun, Changping, Yongping, and Yizhou all have garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan memorialized, "In the ancestral reign there were only the four garrisons of Liaodong, Datong, Xuanfu, and Yansui; then Ningxia and Gansu were added, then Jizhou, then Guyuan and Shanxi; today Miyun, Changping, Yongping, and Yizhou all have garrisons.

sentences.zh: 各鎮防守有主兵。

translations.literal: Each garrison had regular troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Each garrison had regular troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 其後增召募，增客兵，而坐食愈眾。

translations.literal: Later came added recruitment and added guest troops, and those who ate without fighting grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Later came added recruitment and added guest troops, and those who ate rations without fighting grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 各鎮芻餉有屯田。

translations.literal: Each garrison had military colonies for fodder and pay.
translations.idiomatic: Each garrison had military colonies for fodder and pay.

sentences.zh: 其後加民糧，加鹽課，加京運，而橫費滋多。」

translations.literal: Later came added civilian grain levies, added salt duties, added capital transport—and extraneous costs grew ever more."
translations.idiomatic: Later came added civilian grain levies, added salt duties, added capital transport—and extraneous costs grew ever more."

sentences.zh: 因列上隆慶以來歲發之數。

translations.literal: He then listed annual disbursements since Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed annual disbursements since the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「國家歲入不足供所出，而額外陳乞者多。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "State annual income is insufficient for expenditures, yet extraordinary requests are many.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "State annual income is insufficient for expenditures, yet extraordinary requests are many.

sentences.zh: 請以內外一切經費應存革者，刊勒成書。」

translations.literal: I ask that all internal and external expenditures that should be kept or abolished be carved into a book."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all internal and external expenditures that should be kept or abolished be compiled into a book."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 詔市綿二萬五千斤，體乾請俟湖州貢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered 25,000 jin of cotton purchased; Tigan asked to wait for the tribute from Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered twenty-five thousand jin of cotton purchased; Tigan asked to wait for the tribute shipment from Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，趣之急。

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree and urged haste.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree and urged haste.

sentences.zh: 給事中李已言：「三月非用綿時，不宜重擾商戶。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Yi said: "The third month is not the season for cotton use; merchants should not be heavily disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Yi said, "The third month is not the season for cotton use; merchants should not be heavily disturbed."

sentences.zh: 體乾亦復爭，乃命止進萬斤。

translations.literal: Tigan also argued again, and the emperor ordered only 10,000 jin advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan argued again as well, and the emperor ordered only ten thousand jin advanced.

sentences.zh: 逾年，詔趣進金花銀，且購貓睛、祖母綠諸異寶。

translations.literal: A year later an edict urged advance of floral silver and also purchase of cat's-eye, emerald, and other rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: A year later an edict urged advance of floral silver and also purchase of cat's-eye, emerald, and other rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 已上書力諫，體乾請從已言，不納。

translations.literal: Li Yi memorialized forcefully in remonstrance; Tigan asked that his words be followed—the emperor would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi memorialized forcefully in remonstrance; Tigan asked that his words be followed—the emperor would not accept.

sentences.zh: 內承運庫以白劄索部帑十萬。

translations.literal: The inner Chengyun Treasury used an informal white letter to demand 100,000 from the ministry treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The inner Chengyun Treasury used an informal white letter to demand one hundred thousand taels from the ministry treasury.

sentences.zh: 體乾執奏，給事中劉繼文亦言白劄非體。

translations.literal: Tigan held firm in memorial; Supervising Secretary Liu Jiwen also said that white letters were improper form.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan held firm in memorial; Supervising Secretary Liu Jiwen also said that white letters were improper procedure.

sentences.zh: 帝報有旨，竟取之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied that he had his intent and took it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that he had made up his mind and took the funds in the end.

sentences.zh: 體乾又乞承運庫減稅額二十萬，為中官崔敏所格，不得請。

translations.literal: Tigan also asked that the Chengyun Treasury reduce its tax quota by 200,000, but was blocked by the eunuch Cui Min and could not obtain approval.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan also asked that the Chengyun Treasury reduce its tax quota by two hundred thousand, but was blocked by the eunuch Cui Min and could not obtain approval.

sentences.zh: 是時內供已多，數下部取太倉銀，又趣市珍珠黃綠玉諸物。

translations.literal: At this time inner palace supplies were already many; repeatedly the ministry was ordered to take Taicang silver, and pearls, yellow-green jade, and other goods were urgently purchased.
translations.idiomatic: At this time inner palace supplies were already heavy; repeatedly the ministry was ordered to take Taicang silver, and pearls, yellow-green jade, and other goods were urgently purchased.

sentences.zh: 體乾清勁有執，每疏爭，積忤帝意，竟奪官。
